payload.parent_proof_nl: Let x be any real number, and set m = floor(x). By the definition of the floor function, m is an integer, m ≤ x, and m is the greatest integer with this property. We claim that x < m + 1. If not, then x ≥ m + 1. Since m + 1 is also an integer and m + 1 ≤ x, this would contradict the maximality of m as the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Therefore x < m + 1 = floor(x) + 1. Since x was arbitrary, the statement holds for all real x.

domain_restrictions: floor(x) is interpreted as the greatest integer less than or equal to x
parent_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all real x, with k defined as floor(x) (the greatest integer less than or equal to x), it holds that x < k + 1.
